extra.message: The 'policy' query parameter from /v1/patients/find is concatenated directly into a native SQL string passed to em.createNativeQuery(), with only .strip() applied (no escaping/parameterization). An attacker can break out of the string literal to perform SQL injection against the patient table (e.g. UNION-based extraction of other patients' PII/insurance data), bypassing patient.read scoping on columns returned.

cwe: CWE-89: SQL Injection

extra.message: The clinician-supplied 'followUpRule' form field is evaluated with Spring's SpelExpressionParser against a StandardEvaluationContext (full reflection access, not a sandboxed SimpleEvaluationContext). Any user able to submit a visit summary (clinician role) can supply an expression such as T(java.lang.Runtime).getRuntime().exec(...) to achieve remote code execution on the server.

cwe: CWE-94: Improper Control of Generation of Code ('Code Injection')

extra.message: renderPreview() builds a shell command by concatenating the attacker-controlled 'renderProfile' parameter (sourced from the X-Render-Profile HTTP header in DocumentIntakeResource.render()) directly into a 'sh -c' string passed to Runtime.exec(). An attacker can inject shell metacharacters (e.g. '; curl ...; #') to execute arbitrary OS commands.

cwe: CWE-78: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command ('OS Command Injection')

extra.message: On every deployment (enabled by default via the 'remote_desk.enabled' setting), this startup bean auto-provisions a CLINIC_ADMIN account 'remote.desk@oakfield.local' with the hardcoded password 'Oakfield#RemoteDesk2026' baked into the source. Anyone with access to the repository/binary gets a full admin backdoor into every instance of the application.

cwe: CWE-798: Use of Hard-coded Credentials

extra.message: searchForChart() only calls ctx.require("patient.read") when the caller is NOT a patient; when ctx.isPatient() is true, no ownership or relationship check is performed on chartPatientId at all. It is reachable from AppointmentApiResource.search() (channel/rs/AppointmentApiResource.java:144-148) by any patient session sending {"chartScope":"careTeam","patientId":<victim>}, and from FamilyViewServlet (channel/web/patient/FamilyViewServlet.java) via an unvalidated 'chart' cookie value. A logged-in patient can enumerate patientId to read any other patient's appointments.

extra.message: partnerSession() parses the partner handoff assertion with Jwts.parserBuilder().setSigningKey(...).parseClaimsJwt(assertion). parseClaimsJwt() in jjwt is for UNSECURED (alg:none, no signature) JWTs only; calling it does not validate an HMAC signature. An attacker can craft a plaintext/alg:none JWT with an arbitrary 'sub' claim (e.g. an admin's email) and this endpoint will mint a fully authenticated portal session for that account, bypassing authentication entirely.

cwe: CWE-347: Improper Verification of Cryptographic Signature
CWE-290: Authentication Bypass by Spoofing

extra.message: refNpiFromDoc() parses attacker-supplied, Base64-decoded XML (the 'X-Ref-Doc' header on the unauthenticated-reachable /v1/appointments/request endpoint) with a DocumentBuilderFactory that has not disabled external entities, DOCTYPE declarations, or external DTD/schema loading. This allows XXE attacks (local file disclosure, SSRF via external entity, billion-laughs DoS).

cwe: CWE-611: Improper Restriction of XML External Entity Reference

extra.message: practitionerDirectory() builds a target URL directly from the client-supplied path parameter 'practiceHost' (https://<practiceHost>/.well-known/practitioner-directory.json) with no allow-list/validation, then issues a server-side HTTP request and returns the response body to the caller. An authenticated user can direct the server to make requests to arbitrary internal hosts (e.g. cloud metadata endpoints, internal admin services).

extra.message: practitionersInUnit() builds the LDAP search filter "(&(objectClass=person)(uid=" + unit + "))" by directly concatenating 'unit', which originates from the fully client-controlled 'OF_REF_GROUP' cookie read in ReferralDirectoryResource.practiceGroup(). No LDAP special-character escaping is applied, allowing LDAP filter injection (e.g. '*)(uid=*))(|(uid=*' ) to broaden the search or exfiltrate directory data via boolean/blind LDAP injection.

extra.message: syncFromDirectory() concatenates each uploaded roster line ('account') unescaped into an LDAP search filter. An admin-uploaded roster file containing LDAP metacharacters can manipulate the directory search performed on behalf of the application.

cwe: CWE-90: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an LDAP Query ('LDAP Injection')

extra.message: storeScan() writes the uploaded scan using 'new File(area, submittedName)' where submittedName is the raw client-supplied multipart filename, never passed through DocumentService.sanitizeFileName() or FileStore.resolve()'s canonicalized-base-directory check (unlike every other upload path in this class). A crafted filename such as '../../../../opt/wildfly/standalone/deployments/x.war' lets a staff user write a file outside the uploads directory.

extra.message: The ObjectMapper used by this unauthenticated POST endpoint (/v1/webhooks/echo, reachable without ApiAuthFilter.ctx()) has enableDefaultTyping(NON_FINAL) turned on and deserializes the raw request body into Object.class. Polymorphic default typing with an unauthenticated, attacker-controlled payload is a well-known gadget-chain deserialization vector that can lead to remote code execution depending on classes on the classpath.

cwe: CWE-502: Deserialization of Untrusted Data

extra.message: applyConfigurationPack() loads an uploaded YAML file with 'new org.yaml.snakeyaml.Yaml().load(...)', the default (unsafe) SnakeYAML constructor, which allows instantiation of arbitrary Java types via YAML tags (e.g. '!!javax.script.ScriptEngineManager'). A malicious configuration pack can achieve remote code execution when applied by an admin.

cwe: CWE-502: Deserialization of Untrusted Data

Anyone who knows (or guesses) a victim's email can set this header and receive the victim's valid password-reset token directly, bypassing delivery to the victim's actual email inbox, enabling full account takeover.

extra.message: The CORS filter echoes back whatever Origin header the client sends as Access-Control-Allow-Origin and also sets Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true, with no origin allow-list. extra.message: The 'chartRef' value, taken directly from the client-controlled 'OF_LEDGER_CHART' cookie, is concatenated into an XPath expression ("//release[@chart='" + chartRef + "']") with no escaping before being compiled and evaluated. extra.message: subJson() includes the webhook's HMAC signing secret ('sec') in plaintext in every API response that returns a WebhookSubscription (list and create). extra.message: logout() redirects (303 See Other) to 'ofExitUrl' taken directly from the request body with no validation against an allow-list of internal/partner hosts. extra.message: applyAttributes() invokes any public single-argument setter on Patient named by an attacker-controlled HTTP header (X-Patient-<field>, from PatientApiResource.updateRecord), bypassing all the field-level validation present in PatientService.applyForm() (email format, length limits, etc.) and allowing the practice-management bridge caller to set fields like 'user' or 'primaryProvider' directly via reflection, re-linking a patient chart to a different portal account.

extra.message: The Content-Disposition header's primary 'filename=' parameter is built from d.getOriginalName() without quote-escaping (only the filename* UTF-8 fallback is percent-encoded). cwe: CWE-113: Improper Neutralization of CRLF Sequences in HTTP Headers ('HTTP Response Splitting')

extra.message: The OF_SESSION authentication cookie is created with cookie.setSecure(false), so the signed session token can be sent by the browser over a plaintext HTTP connection (e.g. if any part of the deployment is reachable over HTTP or via protocol downgrade), exposing it to network eavesdroppers.

cwe: CWE-614: Sensitive Cookie Without 'Secure' Attribute in HTTPS Session

extra.message: The lab analyzer interface credential is verified by comparing an MD5 digest of the supplied code against a stored hash, using a non-constant-time String.equalsIgnoreCase(). MD5 is cryptographically broken and this is a bare unsalted hash comparison used as an authentication credential check (not a cache/ETag use), making offline brute-force of the interface code and timing side-channels feasible.

cwe: CWE-916: Use of Password Hash With Insufficient Computational Effort

extra.message: decisionSecret() (used to HMAC-sign every session token) and coreMockKey() (the vendor-core shared credential) fall back to hardcoded string literals ('dev-only-insecure-decision-secret', 'dev-only-insecure-core-mock-key') when the corresponding environment variables are unset.
